comments.author: @DollarContourHQ
comments.text: The triple sea divide is probably the most fascinating fact here — rain falling in Czechia can eventually reach three completely different seas. I was also surprised by the medieval fish-pond network in the Třeboň Basin and the fact that the country has over 2,000 castles and fortified ruins. It's incredible how much geography has shaped Czechia's history and landscape.

comments.author: @EveryMileofAmerica
comments.text: The most mind-blowing thing about Czechia is how much its geography has shaped its history. I had no idea that rain falling there can flow toward three different seas, or that Prague is actually farther west than Vienna despite the country often being labeled Eastern Europe. The ancient mountain ring around Bohemia, the underground Punkva River, and the former Iron Curtain zone becoming a wildlife sanctuary were especially fascinating. And over 2,000 castles and fortified ruins? That really puts the country's rugged landscape into perspective. Czechia is far more geographically surprising than most people realize!
